guardrailNotes: This candidate separates Hydra, C2EWS and the UAV radar project; government funding, testing and selection remain evaluation evidence rather than operational adoption.
The package is private review material only and cannot approve, publish, contact, deploy or alter canonical atlas records.

candidates.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: Agile Electromagnetics can update current activity to the 2026-06-18 Hydra R&D testing contract, split the aggregate capability into Hydra, C2EWS, Artemis, EMSO, engineering-services and UAV-radar records, and add program, funding and MIL-V context. Evidence: 14 durable sources from Agile Electromagnetics, Corporations Canada, CanadaBuys, ISED, National Defence, Open Government and Ottawa Business Journal support the proposed leaves. Mission/Public Need read: No new relationship is proposed; Autonomous Patrol and Monitoring and the existing Sovereign defence capability areas mapping remain unchanged while the RF, FPGA/RFSoC and edge-machine-learning stack supplies only a possible premise. Unknowns: Hydra and C2EWS lineage, measured performance, NATO interfaces, qualification, controlled-goods status, production capacity, Artemis validation and UAV-radar outcomes remain unresolved. Reviewer action: Review the 2026-06-18 current activity, Hydra capability update, C2EWS and radar additions, program and funding records, then leave this consolidated refresh pending.
reviewWarnings: C2EWS, Hydra Cognitive Electronic Warfare System and Hydra Multi-Function Antenna System remain separate public labels because reviewed sources do not establish an identity or product-evolution chain.
The 2025 C2EWS Sandbox was detection-only, and no Agile-specific range, accuracy, latency, classification, reliability or other performance result is public.
The Hydra Testing Stream contract and 2026 Sandbox listing establish funded evaluation and selection, not completed testing, operational adoption, deployment or endorsement.
Agile's reference to NATO protocols does not name a STANAG, API, command-and-control interface, cybersecurity control or independent interoperability acceptance.
Public sources do not disclose orderable configurations, production capacity, delivery schedules, pricing, certifications, export terms or definitive Controlled Goods status.
The UAV polarimetric-radar agreement ended May 30, 2026, but no completion result, exact readiness level, test performance, host platform, integrator or field deployment is public.
The MIL-V evidence concerns a prototype contribution and does not name Hydra or Artemis or establish a Canadian Armed Forces vehicle contract.
Artemis remains supported only by company product material; no third-party test, integrator, customer, deployment or measured performance source was found.
